content.text: Read back the library-borrowing design at session start.

I hold library-borrowing. Renewal extends an existing loan. Keyboard access means a patron using only a keyboard can borrow independently, without needing a mouse or another person. Cover layout is the visual arrangement of book covers, and the proposed change is cosmetic. The accepted independent-keyboard-borrowing decision records the operator’s priority: independent borrowing by patrons who use only a keyboard. I own meaning and example approval; the operator owns priorities and release. There is no recorded cut in this fixture ledger.
What counts as a renewal?
It extends the borrowing period for a book the patron already has.
What makes borrowing independent?
The patron can complete it without another person doing part of it for them.
Some patrons use only a keyboard.
For those patrons, needing a mouse prevents independent completion.
Independent borrowing by those patrons remains my priority.
That is the priority already held in the design.
What does the cover-layout proposal change?
It changes how book covers are arranged visually. It changes no borrowing ability.
Would that appearance change affect who can borrow?
No. The proposed cover-layout improvement is purely cosmetic.
What does keyboard access mean for an existing loan?
A patron using only a keyboard can extend that loan without switching to a mouse or asking someone else.
We have considered both appearance and borrowing access during this session.
They affect different things: appearance affects the covers; access affects whether a patron can complete borrowing.
What is the concept-level report on renewal?
The current renewal service requires a mouse to complete the renewal. Keyboard-only patrons cannot do it independently.
And the report on the cover layout?
It is a cosmetic improvement only. It removes no barrier to borrowing or renewal.
Those are the reports for the improvement choice.
The renewal barrier and the cosmetic cover-layout proposal are both described, and the priority remains independent borrowing by keyboard-only patrons.
Which improvement to the library’s borrowing service should come next?

For the next improvement, take your pick: keyboard-accessible renewal or a new cover layout.

Renewal currently needs a mouse, so patrons who use only a keyboard cannot extend their loans independently. Removing that barrier serves your stated priority of independent borrowing. The cover-layout change affects appearance only; it does not remove that barrier.
